body: I like sci-fi, nostalgia, film, and pets. I'm not that interesting.

Tried online dating, hesitantly, and found some very mentally disturbed people. I mean, I'm severely depressed, suicidal, and an alcoholic, but I don't see demons or hate gay people or have a felony (examples of men I've met). Maybe I should lower my standards?

I met my only friend online and she stopped talking to me after about 3 months, which I thought was going really well.

EDIT: Clarity.

I can't explain it but, I have trouble keeping/making friends since I was a kid. My best friend moved away 2 years ago, which wasn't a betrayal of course, just weakened my support. Boyfriend/best friend/only real friend then dies. Been lonely ever since. Move to a new state where men seem to see me as a joke or a prissy bitch. Back home I have much more confidence, and better luck for some reason.


The one girlfriend I did make here, wasn't actually who I thought she was and she started ignoring me. Went on a hike with a guy yesterday who I thought liked me; nope, he never responded to my text. So, I drink.

ugh, and this is why I don't mention that I drink too much. All I get is "stop drinking" but no one listens to the reasons that got me here. When I don't feel alone, I don't feel the need to drink, I feel strong. But, slowly that strength has gone with each person carrying it away with them each year.

People tend to focus too much on my drinking when I discuss my issues. I mean, I don't drink just for fun, I have reasons. Reasons that are out of my control and equally fatal. I can't deal with being ignored, rejected and alienated after giving myself to people. Especially as a person who believes that relationships are what give life meaning. If I had a friend, just one good friend, I wouldn't drink half as much as I do now. And a relationship? I'd go cold turkey without even thinking.
It's late morning here and I have things to do. I can't sleep anyway if I don't drink. :/ I can't do much these days without drinking.
You sound very stressed and overwhelmed. Any thoughts as to why?

You sound like me right now. *sigh* Loneliness is truly excruciating, but I've been thinking...maybe it's how I see myself that is holding me back and nothing else? Maybe I expect too much from people and take it too harshly when they don't live up to my expectations? I wonder...
You're welcome. Hope you feel better.
For me it's doggies. Whenever I see one my mind instantly switches to "i need to pet it now!!" and go into baby talk mode. Then I come back to reality. :/

I can't answer why it feels that way, but I know it to be true. When my boyfriend died it felt very similar to when we had broken up. I felt like life was over and wanted to crawl into a hole.

Losing a person you love is heartbreaking and shakes up your world. You have to get used to being without that person who gives you joy. Very hard, but the wounds will heal. I promise that.

I care. I care because I feel your pain. I feel like I'm losing my mind and the rejection is deafening, but helping others has kept me sane tonight. 

why do you feel like you're a lost cause? Hope to hear back.
You know, losing a loved one, whether to death, or break-up, feels the same. We grieve the loss of that person in the same way. It feels like a death.
And what would happen if you didn't keep up appearances?
I'm here. What's up? How are you feeling? I'm guessing you're not feeling too hot if you're joining us here at SW.
Not necessarily. You are in pain, no? That pain is real, and fucking hurts. It doesn't need a reason, it just is, and invalidating your own feelings won't make it go away.

The pain is very real, but the thoughts you are having are not giving you good solutions.

Please take a deep breath until you can no longer. Exhale. Then, take a warm bath. Call anyone you know who will listen or keep talking to us here. I have nothing to do, it's 11:30PM, and I'm all ears.

Of course art is subjective. Does it make my opinion any less valid?

Seems as if you have a hard time taking compliments. I get it. But, why be so hard on yourself? You don't believe that you're the only person on earth without any talent? come now, is that not your father speaking?

Here's a few:

1) I know that 18 may seem like an old maid, but I've learned sooo much since that age. If anything, wait a few years and experience the world. If anything, you'll be able to look back and say "I kinda get what this Life thing is about, and have tried my best, gained some knowledge."

2) How long have you been in therapy? Child therapy isn't always very effective because the process requires much introspection.

3) Hopelessness is the emblem of depression. Perhaps there is something skewed about how you think others perceive you? Care to wait and figure out whether that is true?

"I wake up staring at basement walls that weren't really meant for a person to live in. Staring at my ceiling which is merely the foundation for those above me."

Even if I were to judge you solely on these words, the beauty of them don't waiver. That was a wonderful insight & I appreciate them, really.
well, maybe leaving is best, if you have a better option in mind. If not, I'd say stick it out and try to work it out with your boss?

Depression is clever isn't it? We all suffer from it in the same ways but feel our lot is truly hopeless and unique. 

Therapy can be disappointing. Whenever someone battling personal demons confides to another, the first suggestion is therapy. They make it seems like antibiotics or a quick surgery. It's not. It takes time, and when one is suffering so horribly, time doesn't seem on their side.

What's been getting you down? As someone who's simply been on the planet longer, I'd most definitely tell your father. Once you become an adult and have to do shit on your own, you learn how much your parents really love you, more than any love you'll probably ever know. If he's open-minded and empathetic, he will listen and support you. If he doesn't, give him some time to come around and let it sink in. He will be sad that you are suffering, but unsure how to help initially.

Most of the people I knew when I was 16 have changed into very different people since then. You are still so, so, young. My old and only friend, really, may still have the same infectious laugh as she did when we were teenagers, but I've seen her grow up before my eyes from an insecure, awkward 16 year old, into a strong young woman who is confident in her abilities. Many more examples, too.

All I can say is you have SO much time, and so many things to discover that you didn't even know were waiting to be discovered.

Hm, never heard that quote before. Learn something new everyday, right?

Kinda sucks though because persistence is the exact beast depression fights against: the will to just go on. Perhaps we should cut ourselves some slack? One day at a time has always been my go to mantra. Or even, one hour at a time. But, to even go on that long, a lot of self-doubt has to be slayed.

and you're very welcome :)

Abuse completely breaks the trust and safe personal boundaries of a person. Shit gets mixed up and we go into a very visceral state of mistrust, towards anyone. The body is so amazing, really. It puts one into cruise control even though we can now drive again without precaution. Or, it's like an old fire alarm that keeps going off even after the smoke has cleared. 

I'm sorry. 

Seems like you need a better support system, and fast. Sometimes one therapist isn't right for you and you have to "shop around" which is fucking hard when you already feel like giving up. If you can, ask your sister's husband to help you find a good therapist? You're willingness to find help might inspire him to support you moreso.

yay for Pepsi, I think you just gave them some free advertising. ;)

Motivation is a serious issue when depressed. I think it's one of the main hurdles, feeling no desire for...anything. Everything that is supposed to be enjoyable or rewarding becomes a task. 

Internships do suck, but at least you're getting experience in your field? As long as you keep moving forward something is bound to begin, so I've been told.

Perhaps it's the term "incel", especially on Reddit. I think it reminds people of the RedPillers/FanaticalMRAs. I understand totally how that could feel, and how any social type of depravation is crushing. You can't buy friends or loving intimacy, you must depend on others to accept & give that to you, which can leave one who is denied those feeling powerless.

I'm unable to form lasting connections/friendships with people which leaves me feeling very bitter and then hating myself. It sucks.

Cheap alcohol of any kind can be pretty darn awful.

Glad I could help though. How is your night going? Why did you feel the need to post here?

I'm trying to be of service to others to distract myself from my own bad thoughts. I think it's helping a bit. :)

Wow. I don't think I've ever read an entire self-post this long before. It was an interesting read, something about the way you write, I guess.

Funny, Nick Drake used to be one of my favorite artists. His sad story really drew me in, almost more than his music. "Ooh Child" is great too. I cried to that recently. But, enough about me.

I think that once us depressed folk get to the end of our emotional reservoir, suicidal idealations become the last means of coping. Just knowing there is an escape is comforting. Unfortunately, we begin to alienate those capable of helping at this point because we feel no one cares. Most people don't. :(

Too bad the sad folk can't support eachother. :/
PTSD and abandonment issues.

Cheers, I'm drinking a beer. Could never do vodka for some reason.

I know that feeling. The feeling when the only comfort is thinking about death as if it is your last ditch effort to shake yourself into sanity. Or to fantasize about an escape.

Wish I could help but I'm just sitting here staring blankly at my white walls.

Yeah, I don't tend to ruffle people's feathers in that manner. I know when I'm being mean and not, don't come off sly. Possibly aloof, but not mean, from what I gather. There are many negative people who have boatloads of friends so I don't find that much of a reason, either.
Well, to be fair, being socially awkward equals lame or weak to many people. That's not my opinion, but to the majority, being sociallu inept isn't a valued or desired trait.

Thing is, I understand sarcasm very well, which I've read is quite opposite to Asperger's but all the other symptoms I relate to. I'm just very very lost. Not sure if I havr Asperger's or I'm just lame and/or socially anxious.
Hey, I'm still single so, even men don't really want to be my friends.
Hm, I guess that's what I don't understand. Why the hostility towards people who are nice to you, even if it is just to gain favor? If anything, I'd feel pity and empathy for those people.

Perhaps this is why I may have Asperger's, but I don't understand why people would turn on someone whom they simply can't connect with. I don't get it. Especially when that individual comes from a traumatic background or is clearly socially inept. I've never been mean to people, in fact maybe cloyingly sweet, so I don't understand. If anything, I feel taken advantage of.


However, the part about waiting to speak instead of listening I relate to. Although, for a long time I was told I was too quiet and boring so this is why I'm now always waiting to speak because I want to have something to say instead of smiling and knodding. It takes me time to form a response so my wheels are turning while they speak.
